facts: The book says people are on 'automatic pilot so much of the time' and 'more asleep than awake, even when we are awake'.
It calls this a 'blanket of unawareness' that may be lethal, rapidly or slowly.
Part III: chapter 19 'Stuck in Stress Reactivity', chapter 20 'Responding to Stress Instead of Reacting'.
Habitual, automatic reactions to stressors determine in large measure how much stress we experience.
Part I covers mindfulness of daily activities such as eating; Part IV includes seeing a headache as 'just a headache' rather than 'my headache'.
One critical reader finds the portrait of everyday unawareness overdrawn.
scene_details: A headache seen as 'just a headache'.
Chapter titles about reacting and responding.
tension: The book says a big share of our stress comes from reactions we never notice making.
opening_idea: Open on the book's phrase 'more asleep than awake'.
